classification.habit: Small evergreen tree, 6–15 m tall, coppiced in cultivation as a bushy shrub.
classification.habitat: Tropical evergreen forests and plantations on sandy, well-drained soil in humid climates.
classification.distribution: Native to Sri Lanka and South India; cultivated in Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu (Western Ghats).

identification.description: Thin inner bark, usually in rolled or quilled pieces, yellowish-brown and strongly aromatic.
identification.whole_plant: Aromatic evergreen tree with thick, leathery, opposite, three-nerved leaves and small yellowish flowers in panicles.
identification.stem: Woody stem with thick, aromatic bark; young shoots of coppiced plants provide the drug.
identification.leaf: Opposite, ovate to elliptic, coriaceous leaves 7–18 cm long with three prominent longitudinal nerves; young leaves reddish; aromatic when crushed.
identification.flower: Small, pale yellowish, silky flowers in axillary or terminal panicles.
identification.fruit: Ovoid, dark purple, one-seeded berry about 1–1.5 cm long, seated on an enlarged perianth cup.
identification.bark: Dried inner bark, about 0.5 mm thick, in single or double compound quills; outer surface dull yellowish-brown with pale wavy lines, inner surface darker; fracture splintery; fragrant odour; sweet, aromatic taste with warmth (API).
identification_points: Thin, brittle bark in packed compound quills
Dull yellowish-brown outer surface with pale wavy lines

therapeutics.precautions: Ushna-Tikshna drug: use in small doses and cautiously in Pitta disorders and bleeding states. Cassia bark (C. cassia) has much higher coumarin than true cinnamon; prolonged high doses should be avoided.
therapeutics.contraindications: Raktapitta and bleeding disorders, Pitta-predominant conditions with burning, pregnancy in medicinal doses, and known cinnamon allergy.

shlokas: त्वक्पत्रञ्च वराङ्गं स्याद् भृङ्गं चोचं तथोत्कटम् ॥६४॥

त्वचं लघूष्णं कटुकं स्वादु तिक्तञ्च रूक्षकम् ।
पित्तलं कफवातघ्नं कण्ड्वामारुचिनाशनम् ।
हृद्बस्तिरोगवातार्शः कृमिपीनसशुक्रहृत् ॥६५॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The aroma and taste come from the essential oil, mainly cinnamaldehyde with some eugenol; tannins and mucilage are also present (API).

modern_information.evidence_summary: Stimulates digestion, circulation and balances kapha dosha.
modern_information.safety_notes: Safe in culinary amounts; concentrated oil can irritate skin and mucosa, and cassia-type bark used in high doses for long periods may affect the liver because of coumarin.

exam_points: Botanical name: Cinnamomum verum J.Presl (syn. C. zeylanicum); Family: Lauraceae
Rasa: Katu, Tikta, Madhura; Guna: Laghu, Ruksha, Tikshna; Virya: Ushna; Vipaka: Katu
Member of Trijata (Twak, Ela, Patra) and Chaturjata (+ Nagakeshara)
viva_questions: Give the botanical name and family of Twak.
Which part of the plant is Twak and how is it identified?
What is the chief constituent of cinnamon bark oil?
mnemonics: Trijata = Twak + Ela + Tejapatra; add Nagakeshara for Chaturjata
student.quick_revision: Stimulates digestion, circulation and balances kapha dosha.

teaching_points: Distinguish true cinnamon (C. verum) from cassia (C. cassia).
Use Twak to teach bark as a crude drug.
discussion_points: Adulteration of Twak with cassia bark
Coumarin content and safety of cinnamon products
practical_points: Compare quills of true cinnamon and cassia by thickness, colour and taste.

doctor.quick_reference: Twak (inner bark of Cinnamomum verum; Katu-Tikta-Madhura, Ushna) is a Kaphavatahara, Ruchya and Mukhashodhana drug used in Kasa, Pinasa, Agnimandya and mouth disorders; 1–3 g churna.
key_precautions: Caution in Pitta and bleeding states
Avoid high medicinal doses in pregnancy
Avoid prolonged high doses of cassia-type bark
